* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and rough surf.

* WHERE...The beaches of Volusia, Brevard, Indian River, Saint
Lucie, and Martin Counties.

* WHEN...Through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.instruction:

from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and

shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

For the Coastal Flood Statement, isolated minor coastal
flooding expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Broward County and Coastal Miami Dade County.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Friday evening.
For the Coastal Flood Statement, from 3 AM EDT Wednesday
through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Some water on low lying roads and property. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor coastal flooding is expected around
high tide.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

protect property.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 20 at 12:37AM MST until October 22 at 11:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...All of northern and central Arizona.

* WHEN...From late tonight through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry
washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An upper-level trough will bring a deep surge of subtropical and
tropical moisture into our region. Showers and thunderstorms will
develop across much of northern and central Arizona early
Wednesday morning and continue through Thursday evening. Stronger
thunderstorms will bring threats of Flash Flooding, while more
prolonged rainfall could lead to elevated flow in streams,
rivers, and washes.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Have a way to receive Flash Flood Warnings and be prepared to take
action should warnings be issued.
